title: playable-screen-38of38-fastpaths1010-scope
queue_order: One binary (this lane's step-1 commit, ref 7002282149, same as step 2 and step 3), env-only A/B per title: ON queues with no --env (app default, all three switches on); OFF queues --env HAKUX_POSTED_PUT=0 --env HAKUX_LOCKFREE_WAKE=0 --env HAKUX_SUBMIT_FRAMES=2 (the pre-lane shipped values). Scope: the 38 titles fastpaths1010's own step 3 screened and actually ran (its PR.md table, 39 rows minus Call of Duty 3's 'not run' row) -- the brief's text says '37 titles fastpaths1010 screened' but the ground truth in fastpaths1010/PR.md is 38 run + 1 not-run (Call of Duty 3); RalliSport was already excluded from fastpaths1010's own scope, and the five owner-deferred titles (Azurik, Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance, NBA Live 2004, Castlevania: Curse of Darkness, 50 Cent: Bulletproof) stay off per that lane's Addendum 3, carried forward unchanged. 10 titles carry their own named route (300s, no --frames-every, since a scored route supplies its own mark/shot frames): Crimson Skies (crimson-skies), Spikeout (spikeout), Jet Set Radio Future (jsrf), Tork (tork), Kabuki Warriors (kabuki-warriors), 187: Ride or Die (187-ride-or-die), Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2x (thps2x), KOF: Maximum Impact - Maniax (kof-mi), Alien Hominid (alien-hominid), WWE Raw 2 (wwe-raw-2). 28 titles run as a soak to the title screen, 180s, --frames-every 15. ISO filenames and route/soak plan are fastpaths1010/NOTES.md sections 4.1.2/4.3/4.4's own, copied verbatim (docs/lanes/nfsdefault1011/NOTES.md section 4 restates the full table). One run per arm per title (not two): a screen catches a correctness regression, not a precise pace measurement; a title that fails gets rerun twice before any attribution, per the brief. Device presence is not re-verified by a live listing before queuing (none exists) -- fastpaths1010's own screen found titles can go missing without notice (12 of 21 once), so a 'title not on device' on any of these 38 is possible despite all having run clean under fastpaths1010 within the last day, and is treated as a per-title blocker (moved to not_run, not fail_titles), not grounds to distrust the batch. Queued in batches of about 10 titles (per the brief), HAKUX_RELEASE_PRIO=1, ON then OFF per title.

judge: per-title, by eye plus docs/lanes/nfsdefault1011/screenread.py <run_dir> [...] (title_verdict.judge() for booted/reached_gameplay/crash/void/gfps; route-frames or --frames-every captures reviewed where present): fatal (crash/hang/abort logcat ON that OFF does not show), frames (region comparison, ON vs OFF, where captures exist), gfps (hakuX-pace-derived g_fps_mean_reported_not_judged, ON vs OFF). No reports column (fastpaths1010's four on-lines already proved the switches reach native in step 2/3; this screen is for correctness, not re-proving plumbing per title). No single numeric threshold applies across 38 different titles -- each title's row is read against its own OFF baseline, recorded in docs/lanes/nfsdefault1011/NOTES.md and PR.md's screen table.
baseline: Every one of these 38 titles already has a clean ON/OFF pass from fastpaths1010's own step 3 screen (its PR.md table) with the six-switch 'Fast renderer paths' toggle; this screen adds the two pfifo switches and SUBMIT_FRAMES=3 on top of that already-accepted toggle. A title regressing between ON and OFF here would be a regression from this lane's step 1 commit specifically (the two pfifo switches or the submit_frames default change), not a pre-existing fastpaths1010 issue.
prediction: None of the 38 fail. postput1010 and lockwake1011 already screened HAKUX_POSTED_PUT/HAKUX_LOCKFREE_WAKE narrowly (NFS MW, a cross-title screen ranked P 0.6 but not yet run broadly); coldstart1010 already screened HAKUX_SUBMIT_FRAMES=3 on some titles without a correctness regression. Step 3's own Simpsons free-roam A/B (GPU-paced, the title postput1010's PR.md specifically worried about) passed clean. What would refute it: any ON-only crash/hang/abort; any ON-only visual defect in a frame region OFF does not show; a gfps gap wider than fastpaths1010's own typical <1%, in the direction of a regression (not Kabuki Warriors' noted-but-not-escalated 6% gap, which was a single-sample route-run variance fastpaths1010 chose not to escalate).
expect_note: fail_titles starts empty: the claim under test is that no SCOPED title fails. not_run carries forward Call of Duty 3 (confirmed not on the Nova by fastpaths1010's own live check) unchanged -- this lane does not re-probe it. blocked_titles carries forward the five owner-deferred titles plus RalliSport (excluded by this lane's own brief), none of which block marking this lane's PR ready unless a WIDEN: defect found elsewhere in the 38 leads lane.local to pull one in. A title failing live with 'title not on device' (fastpaths1010's own experience: 12 of 21 once) moves to not_run, not fail_titles -- it never produced an ON-vs-OFF correctness result to fail. A confirmed defect (fails fatal/frames/gfps after two reruns) gets a NOTES.md line starting WIDEN:, naming the title/column/result ids, and per the brief's isolation rule, this lane reruns that one title with each of the three switches set back individually (at most three runs) before deciding which switch to drop from the default.
